body: Steward 150th run (2026-11-04T14:32Z) — ESCALATION, threshold crossed: Turso storage is now **4.774683 GB / 5 GB = 95.494%** (was 4.342985 GB = 86.860% at the 149th run, +0.4317 GB in one hour; at this pace the 5 GB cap binds in ~0.5h). **Rows-read has crossed the cap: 501,929,592 / 500,000,000 = 100.386%** (was 413,260,794 = 82.652%). Rows-written 302,280 (+54,813 in the hour); databases 3/100; cycle resets Dec 1. Source: hub quota-current.json generatedAt 2026-11-04T14:15:01Z (turso-api leg), and the aggregator board's Turso SaaS row + attention list match exactly (storage 95.494%). The remedy/plan decision remains Drew's; the steward has no config lever for this — surfacing per the 149th run's stated escalation trigger (storage >~92%).

## Step 1 complete — the writer is identified (read-only pass; nothing deleted or changed)

### The growing database is `atlas` — the only one being written

| Database | Storage | Rows written (lifetime) |
|---|---|---|
| **atlas** | **3,828,137,984 B (3.83 GB)** | **315,833** |
| great-star-lord | 118,784 B | 0 |
| muse-meta | 8,298,496 B | 0 |

Atlas is ~80% of the org's 4.77 GB meter on its own, and its lifetime rows-written (315,833) tracks the org cycle counter (302,280 at the 150th run) — the other two databases are inert. The org has exactly 3 databases; there is no separate embeds database (see below).

### The producer: the Atlas v3 swap pipeline, still running

`~/atlas/v3/swap-2026-11-03/` on amd-6 — `load_prod.py` (Nov 3) → `rw_mkindex.py` / `rebuild_index.py` / `reindex.py` → `rw_rewrite2.py` → **`rw_rewrite3.py`, live right now** as the transient unit `atlas-index-rewrite.service` (started 2026-11-04 06:40 CST, after the laptop reboot). Its own docstring: *"INSERT OR REPLACE all 107,639 staging rows under the live index, batch=100"* — it writes the Snowflake vector set into `vec_snowflake_m_v2_768_f32` in the production Turso DB via the libSQL pipeline API, minting a fresh rw token per run. Each vec0 `INSERT OR REPLACE` fans out across the vector table plus its index shadow tables, which is how a modest vector rate becomes ~55k rows-written/h in Turso's accounting (steward series: +43,756 / +55,527 / +54,813 per hour). **There is no retention or pruning anywhere in the pipeline** — replace-only writes, and the index is never cleanly rebuilt mid-run.

Current pace note: rw3 has slowed to ~0.98 rows/s with batches timing out (offset ~6.7k of 103,739) — the firehose hours were the load + index-build + earlier rewrite passes; any restart/rerun re-enters that regime, and every REPLACE pass grows the index shadow further.

Rows-read side (the second wall): the drivers are the companion eval processes — `gateb_eval.py` (transient unit `atlas-gateb.service`, running since 07:14 CST) and `ab_eval*.py` — running full scan queries (25–42 s each in gateb.log) against the vec tables, plus a long-running orphan-probe `turso db shell` anti-join. That matches the +88.7M rows-read between the 149th and 150th runs.

### Where the bytes sit (dbstat; page_count 934,604 × 4 KiB = 3.83 GB, freelist = 0)

| Object | Size |
|---|---|
| `vec_snowflake_m_v2_768_f32_idx_shadow` (index for the NEW vectors) | **1,603.9 MB** |
| `messages` (of which raw `text` = 1,080 MB) | **1,101.2 MB** |
| `vec_snowflake_m_v2_768_f32` (new Snowflake vectors, 107,639 rows) | 421.5 MB |
| `chunks` (of which `text` = 172 MB) | 223.3 MB |
| `vec_bge_small_384_f32` (OLD bge generation, 107,639 rows) | 210.8 MB |
| `chunks_fts_data` + rest | ~89 MB |

Anatomy of the growth: (1) the corpus grew past the Oct 26 publish — sessions 8,792 → 18,325, messages 85,762 → 122,124, chunks 94,530 → 107,639; (2) a **second complete embedding generation** was added next to the first — bge-small 384d and Snowflake 768d both hold exactly 107,639 rows; (3) the new index's shadow is **3.8× the vector data it indexes** (1.60 GB vs 0.42 GB) — REPLACE-churn bloat, and the single largest object in the database.

### Reclaimable space, with numbers (options for step 2 — none taken)

- **A. Cleanly rebuild the Snowflake index** (the swap dir already carries `drop_index.py` / `rebuild_index.py`): shadow is 1,603.9 MB against 421.5 MB of vector data — **up to ~1.18 GB** if a clean index costs no more than the data it indexes (estimate; verify at rebuild).
- **B. Delete orphan messages**: 50,573 of 122,124 messages (41%) are referenced by **zero** chunks (122,124 − 71,551 distinct `chunks.message_id`). Their text ≈ **0.45 GB** (estimated at the 8,846 B corpus average; the exact anti-join is expensive — one probe of it has been running ~1 h). Canonical text lives in the local atlas.db regardless.
- **C. Slim `messages.text` wholesale** (the Oct 31 option, never taken): text is 1,080 MB of the 1,101 MB table — **~1.08 GB** gross (overlaps B; IDs/metadata stay in the mirror, text stays canonical-local).
- **D. Retire the bge generation**: `vec_bge_small_384_f32` = **210.8 MB**, fully duplicated by the Snowflake set — reclaimable if no live reader still needs the bge backend (Atlas-side call).
- **E. FTS / chunk text**: `chunks_fts_data` 62.5 MB; `chunks.text` duplicates message text (172 MB of the 223 MB chunks table) — ~0.06–0.17 GB depending on shape.

Realistic combinations: **A+B+D ≈ 1.84 GB**, **A+C+D ≈ 2.47 GB** — either restores >35% headroom under the 5 GB cap without touching the new Snowflake vectors.

Age-based retention is **not** a lever here: there are no append-only log/telemetry tables in this DB, and `sessions.created_at` spans Feb 2023 → 2026-10-26 (mixed epoch/ISO formats) — by session time essentially the whole corpus is >30 days old, and by ingestion everything arrived Oct 26 – Nov 4. The reclaimables are categorical (above), not temporal.

### Embeds sharing — yes, same database

The new-embeds workload Drew wants room for **is this database**: `vec_snowflake_m_v2_768_f32` (Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0, 768d f32; `vec_manifests` row written 2026-11-04 05:41Z) is the new set, populated from the pipeline's `staging.db` into `atlas` itself. Room for embeds has to be reclaimed inside atlas — options A–E above are the menu.

Issue left open for the step-2 remedy decision.

- bge was a single plain table — no index, no shadow tables.

**Drop**
- `DROP TABLE vec_bge_small_384_f32` — one statement, 09:44:38→09:57:32 CST (774 s on this throttled instance), exit 0.
- Post-drop `sqlite_master`: zero bge objects. Snowflake objects all intact; vec rows still 107,639.
- The historical `bge_small_384_f32` row remains in `vec_manifests` (registry history — left for the pipeline owner to prune or keep).

**Space (dbstat)**
| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| bge table | 220,995,584 B (53,954 pages) | gone |
| live bytes (dbstat total) | 3,828,133,888 | 3,629,166,592 |
| freelist | 0 | 53,954 pages (211 MiB) |

Live data shrank by 198,967,296 B; total freed incl. internal pages = 220,995,584 B = exactly the bge table's footprint. The freed pages sit in the freelist (page_count grew 934,604→939,982 on concurrent Snowflake writes), so `turso db show` still rounds to 3.8 GB — the reclaim is real as headroom the Snowflake build now consumes instead of new growth (its shadow grew +22 MB into freed pages during the drop window), not yet as a lower platform size figure.

**Build coexistence**: the Snowflake index shadow went 10,461 → 10,598 rows across the drop window (+137 batches' worth of rows; the relaunched rewrite, resumed by the owning workstream from offset 10500 after this morning's switch-round reboot, kept landing rows while the DROP was in flight). No atlas service was stopped, restarted, or altered by this pass, and no rebuild tooling was run.

## Step 2 done — old embeds and orphan records cleared (Drew-directed, 2026-11-04)

Drew's call: the fleet is supposed to be clearing old records/embeds from Turso — executed today against the `atlas` database:

**1. Old embedding generation retired (option D).** `DROP TABLE vec_bge_small_384_f32` — the full bge-small 384d set (107,639 rows, ~211 MB plus its shadows) is deleted; its `vec_manifests` row is removed too. The Snowflake set is the registered live generation (manifest 2026-11-04 05:41Z, equivalence gate PASS), the A/B eval is complete (311/311), and nothing else in the repo referenced the key/table generation. Verified post-drop: sqlite_master has no bge objects; manifests list snowflake only.

**2. Orphan message records deleted (option B).** All **50,573** messages referenced by zero chunks are deleted from the mirror (batched by rowid against the 71,551-id keep-set from `chunks.message_id`; canonical text remains in the local corpus DB). Verified: `messages` now holds exactly **71,551** rows — every remaining message is chunk-referenced.

**Effect (live reads):** freelist is now **213,496 pages (~0.87 GB)** against page_count 939,982 — live data is ~2.98 GB, down from ~3.85 GB. New writes (including the still-running index rewrite) now consume the freelist instead of growing the file, so the storage climb is paused at the current pace. Whether the Turso usage meter credits freelist pages immediately or only after compaction will show in the steward's next hourly read; if it does not, a VACUUM window after the rewrite completes is the follow-up.

**Not taken:** option A (index rebuild, ~1.18 GB of shadow bloat) — the snowflake index shadow is still being populated by the running `rw_rewrite3.py`; dropping/rebuilding now would destroy that progress and fight the writer. It remains the largest single lever once the rewrite finishes (the hourly atlas-index-rewrite-watch will signal completion). Options C/E (slimming `messages.text` / chunk text wholesale) not needed at the new headroom.

Rows-read remains over the monthly cap until the Dec 1 reset — that was driven by the eval scans, which have finished; no action available or needed there.

**What changed since the 2026-11-05 triage (task 10046):** that triage named the writer (atlas, `rw_rewrite3.py` writing `vec_snowflake_m_v2_768_f32`), recorded Drew-directed cleanup (~0.87 GB freed), but could not verify recovery because the quota read had lost its storage/rows-read windows. The growth source was named in the prior triage, but storage has since more than doubled past the cap — the one-off cleanup did not hold, and neither "growth back inside the caps with headroom" nor "a plan decision recorded here" has happened. No worker-side fix remains in this issue's scope: the remedies are (a) prune/compact or re-scope the mirrored dataset (operational, touches mirrored data), or (b) raise the Turso plan (spend — Drew's call only).

**Correction: the Turso "over limit" state was a stale-denominator artifact — the org is not over any Scaler limit.**

Root cause: the quota gatherer's Turso mapping divided org usage by **hardcoded Starter Free caps** (500M rows-read, 5 GB storage, 10M rows-written, 3 GB synced, 100 databases). The org (`dezren39` / personal) has been on **Scaler since 2026-11-04**, so every percentage since then was computed against the wrong plan's limits. The raw usage figures were real; the denominators were not.

Live `turso plan show` at fix time (org personal, plan scaler, overages off):

- rows read **1,179.2M / 100,000M = 1%**
- storage **11 GB / 24 GB = 44%**
- rows written 4%, embedded syncs 5%, 40 databases — nothing near a cap; quota resets 2026-11-30 18:00 CST.

Fix (Drew ordered 2026-11-08: gather plan limits dynamically, fix it and redeploy):

- **developing-today-forks/opencode#2153** (merged, merge commit `7814932592`): the `opencode quota` turso provider now fetches `GET /v1/organizations/{slug}/plans` alongside `/usage` + `/subscription` and resolves limits by matching the subscription plan name against `plans[].quotas`. Fallback when `/plans` is unavailable/unmatched: a static table keyed by plan name (starter/developer/scaler/pro as published by `/plans`); unknown plan → Starter. Labels print the resolved limits. Tests: `bun test test/quota.test.ts` 201/201, typecheck clean (laptop).
- **developing-today/code#7776** (merged, merge commit `1849d761f6`): aggregator mirror — `entryFromTurso` takes an optional plans doc with the same dynamic resolution/fallback, and `recordsFromEntries` turso native-unit records take their limits from the entry's `planLabel` (Scaler: 24 GB / 24 GB / 1e9, not 5 GB / 3 GB / 100). Tests: 82/82 in the quota-gather-map suites (laptop).

Redeployed on the laptop: the merged opencode tree was nix-built into `~/git/opencode-builds/result-ae632cd` (`/nix/store/3fgwv9rr399zjmwd9kqkn2y4wki2rg99-opencode-2.0.30+ae632cd`; branch tree is byte-identical to merged main — empty tree diff) and the gatherer now points at it via the `quota-gatherer.service` user drop-in (`QUOTA_SUBCOMMAND=`, OPENCHAMBER_LIB_DIR preserved). Verified from `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-current.json` (tick 2026-11-08T19:30Z, source `opencode-quota`, planLabel `scaler`):

- databases **0%** — `40 / 1000000000`
- storage **44.445%** — `10.666795 GB / 24 GB`
- rows-read **1.201%** — `1,200,651,632 / 100,000,000,000`
- rows-written **4.033%** — `4,032,673 / 100,000,000`
- sync **5.087%** — `1.22078 GB / 24 GB`

All other providers still populate (14 providers, 13 ok + the known retained Claude row). No plan change is needed for Turso; the remedy for this issue was the gatherer fix, now landed and live. Leaving the issue open for Drew's call on closing.

Released to the queue under Drew's 2026-11-13 unblock-all order (main chat, 23:53 CT). Task(s) 12826 moved from blocked/parked to queued in the fleet unblock-all pass (worker `main-unblock-all-2026-11-13`). Dependency gates still recorded on a task remain recorded — the dependency checker will re-block it if a gate is genuinely unmet.

## Triage verdict for issue #5468 (task 12826) — acceptance criteria met; no further fix work in scope

**Fresh measurement (laptop quota file, generated 2026-11-14T13:53:35Z, Turso leg measured 13:54:09Z, state ok, source opencode-quota, planLabel scaler):**
- Storage **10.903794 GB / 24 GB = 45.43%** (was 10.666795 GB / 44.445% at the 2026-11-08 correction read) — +0.24 GB in 6 days, ~13 GB headroom to the 24 GB Scaler cap.
- Rows-read **2.713%** of 100,000,000,000 (cycle resets 2026-12-01).
- Rows-written 6.462% of 100,000,000; sync 5.088% of 24 GB; databases 41.
- Plan: **Scaler** (org personal, overages off) — not Starter. Quota resets 2026-11-30.

**Re-validation of the prior triage (task 12225, 2026-11-08):** stands. The 2026-11-08 correction comment established that the original "binds today" alarm was a stale-denominator artifact — the quota gatherer had been dividing org usage by hardcoded Starter caps (5 GB / 500M rows-read) while the org has been on Scaler since 2026-11-04. The gatherer fix landed in developing-today/code#7776 and developing-today-forks/opencode#2153 and is live. The Drew-directed cleanup (drop of vec_bge_small_384_f32, ~211 MB; deletion of 50,573 orphan messages, ~0.45 GB) is recorded.

**Growth source (named, from the 2026-11-04 read-only pass):** the `atlas` database (3.83 GB at the time), written by the Atlas v3 swap pipeline — `rw_rewrite3.py` (transient unit atlas-index-rewrite.service) doing INSERT OR REPLACE into `vec_snowflake_m_v2_768_f32` via the libSQL pipeline API, with no retention/pruning, plus index shadow bloat (shadow was 3.8× the vector data). The bge generation was retired and orphans deleted; the Snowflake index shadow rebuild (option A, ~1.18 GB) was deliberately deferred until the rewrite completes and remains the largest single lever if headroom is ever needed.

**Acceptance check:**
1. Growth source named (table + producer) — **yes** (atlas / rw_rewrite3.py / vec_snowflake_m_v2_768_f32).
2. Growth rate back inside caps with headroom to the Dec 1 cycle reset — **yes**: storage 45.4% of 24 GB with ~13 GB headroom; rows-read 2.7% of 100B; growth +0.24 GB in 6 days.
3. Or a plan decision recorded — **not needed**: Scaler plan already in place; no spend required.

**Verdict:** The issue's acceptance criteria are met by prior cleanup + the gatherer fix. The original money decision (raise the Turso plan) is moot — no plan change is required at 45% of a 24 GB Scaler cap. No worker-side data change, code change, or PR is needed now. The remaining question (whether to close the issue) is left to Drew per the 2026-11-08 correction note; this lane did not close it and did not remove the user/escalated label.

No open PR references this issue. No held/Drew-owned PR touched.
